cards.text: At Babel, the LORD just scattered the people over the face of all the earth (Genesis 11:9). Now Genesis follows one family line, the account of Shem, Noah’s son (Genesis 5:32).

Two years after the flood, Shem becomes the father of Arphaxad, and then it’s son after son: Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, and Nahor, who becomes the father of Terah. Each man has his son, lives on for years, and has other sons and daughters. Shem lives 500 more years after Arphaxad is born, and by the time we get to Nahor it’s 119, which, friend, is the SHORT one!
When Terah is 70, he becomes the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran. Yes, ANOTHER Nahor, so somebody yells “NAHOR!” at the family reunion and two heads turn.

cards.question: Terah’s son Haran has a son of his own. What’s his name?

cards.text: Then hard news: while his father Terah is still alive, Haran dies in his native land, Ur of the Chaldeans. I think this one hurts.

cards.question: Terah’s sons Abram and Nahor both take wives. Abram’s wife is named ___.
Nahor’s wife is named Milcah. True or false: she’s the daughter of Terah’s son Haran, the one who died in Ur.
Genesis has listed sons and daughters for man after man. True or false: Abram and Sarai have children too.

cards.text: After all those sons and daughters, this line lands heavy: Sarai is barren, with no children. Then Terah packs up his family and sets out from Ur of the Chaldeans.

cards.question: Terah’s family sets out from Ur of the Chaldeans, headed for the land of ___.
Lot’s father Haran has died. True or false: Terah brings his grandson Lot along on the trip.
Terah’s family is headed for Canaan. But where do they stop and settle?

cards.text: Terah lives 205 years, and he dies in Haran.
Then the LORD speaks to Abram, and it’s a BIG ask. Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household.

cards.question: God tells Abram to leave it all behind. Where is Abram supposed to go?

answers.text: To a land God will show him
East to the land of Shinar
Down to the land of Egypt

cards.text: That’s like packing your whole life into the car and typing “I’ll know it when I see it” into the GPS. Then God starts making Abram promises, and they are HUGE.

cards.question: Sarai has no children. But what does God promise to make Abram into?
True or false: God promises to make Abram’s name great.

cards.text: God says He’ll bless Abram so that Abram will be a blessing. He’ll bless those who bless Abram and curse those who curse him.

cards.question: God has one last promise for Abram. Who does He say will be blessed through him?

answers.text: All the families of the earth

cards.question: God has made Abram huge promises and still hasn’t named the land. True or false: Abram goes, just as the LORD told him.

cards.text: So Abram leaves Haran at seventy-five years old with Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all the possessions and people they’d acquired there, headed for Canaan. When the angel called me out of that junk drawer I packed ZERO bags, and this man is moving a WHOLE household!

cards.question: Terah’s trip stopped in Haran. True or false: this time, Abram makes it all the way to the land of Canaan.

cards.text: He MAKES it, friend! Abram travels through the land as far as the Oak of Moreh at Shechem.

cards.question: True or false: when Abram gets there, the land of Canaan is empty, with nobody else living in it.

cards.text: The Canaanites are already in the land, like pulling up to your new place and finding somebody’s car already in the driveway. Then the LORD appears to Abram with a promise about this land.

cards.question: The LORD makes Abram a promise about this land. Who does He say He’ll give it to?
Right there, Abram builds something to the LORD, who appeared to him. What is it?
From there, Abram moves to the hill country east of Bethel and pitches his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. True or false: he builds another altar to the LORD there.

cards.text: There he calls on the name of the LORD, and then he journeys on toward the Negev. Abram’s on the move, friend, and this road has a whole lot more miles in it.
